full_judgment:
Quazi Reza-ul-Hoque J: The instant Rule was issued on 24-10-2013 calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Memo dated 9-10-2013 (annexure-H) shall not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect, and why they shall not be directed to promote the petitioner to the post of Chief Engineer (PWD) on the basis of seniority and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. And pending hearing of the Rule, there was an order of injunction from promoting any junior of the petitioner in the post of Chief Engineer (PWD) for a period of 6(six) months. 

 2. The facts necessary for disposal of the Rule, as has been stated by the petitioner, in short, is that the petitioner was appointed by the respondent No. 1, as an Assistant Engineer of Public Works Department (PWD) and, accordingly, the petitioner joined the said post on 9-3-1979, and in course of his service he has been promoted to different posts from time to time (Annexure-A). The respondent No. 1 by the Notification being No. GriGoMo/Sha-1/5A-2/2009/131 dated 3-11-2010 promoted, amongst others, the petitioner from the post of Superintending Engineer to the Additional Chief Engineer (Civil) (Annexure-B). 

 3. The post of Chief Engineer under PWD has been vacant since 17-8-2011 and hence, it was bonafide and legitimate expectation of the petitioner, who is one of the senior Additional Chief Engineers of PWD, that he will be promoted to the post of Chief Engineer under PWD. And to the utter surprise of all and notwithstanding that there were other senior eligible candidates available for consideration of promotion for the post of Chief Engineer under PWD, the respondent No. 1 by the Notification being No. GriGoMo/Sha-I/5A-3/2009/91 dated 17-8-2011 assigned the additional charge to one personnel, namely, Md. Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan, to perform the current functions of Chief Engineer under PWD. Subsequently, the respondent No. 1 by the Notification being No. GriGoMo /Sha-1/4P-1 /2011/104 dated 22-9-2011 posted the aforesaid personnel, namely, Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan (the said Current Charge holder) in the post of Chief Engineer (Current Charge) of PWD (Annexures-C and C-1). 

 4. The respondent No. 1 had earlier by the Notification being No. 25.013.2012.05.003.2010-69 dated 30-6-2011 promoted, amongst others, the said Current Charge holder to the post of Additional Chief Engineer (Civil) from the post of superintending Engineer, whilst the petitioner is senior to the said Current Charge-holder and enlisted at Serial No. 128 of the Gradation List of PWD, while the said Current Charge-holder is enlisted at Serial No. 133 of the Gradation List (Annexures-D and D-1). 

 5. The respondent No. 1 by the Notification 18-10-2012 posted the said Current Charge-holder as Director (Current Charge) of Housing and Building Research Institute, Dams Salam, Mirpur, Dhaka, thus removing him from the post of Chief Engineer (current Charge) under PWD and, simultaneously, another personnel, namely, Khondokar Salahuddin and enlisted at serial No. 127 of the gradation list of PWD (who is senior to the said Current Charge-holder), was assigned the post of Chief Engineer (Current Charge) under PWD. Subsequently, the respondent No. 1 by the Notification being No. 25.013.011.05.00.003.2009-09 dated 28-1-2013 again posted the said current Charge-holder as Chief Engineer (Current Charge) of PWD (Annexures-E and E-1). 

 6. In order to consider proposal for promotion for the post of Chief Engineer under PWD, the respondent No. 1 by the Memo being No. 25.00.0000.013.12.003.09-533 dated 13-8-2013 made an enquiry before the Anti-Corruption Commission, Head Office, Dhaka to provide information as to whether there were any corruption-related allegations or cases against the top 7(seven) officials of PWD which included the petitioner and the said current Charge-holder at Serial Nos. 3 and 7 respectively (Annexure- F); and in reply to the aforesaid Memo dated 13-8-2013 issued by respondent No. 1 the Anti-Corruption Commission, Head Office, Dhaka by Memo being No. DuDoK/ProSha: O LoGi: /35/2007 (Ongsho-3)/26006 dated 18-9-2013 stated that there were no allegation, inquiry, investigation or case pending against the said top 7 (seven) officials of PWD (Annexure-G). 

 7. In the meantime, the respondent No. 1 by the impugned Memo being No. 25.00.0000.013.12.001.09-678 dated 9-10-2013 submitted a summary for Superior Selection Board (SSB) for promotion for the post of Chief Engineer under PWD. It is evident from the said Memo dated 9-10-2013 that only the name of the said Current Charge-holder was proposed to the SSB for promotion for the post of Chief Engineer under PWD, although there were 6(six) personnel (including the petitioner) who were eligible for promotion, who are senior to the said Current Charge-holder (Annexure-H). 

 8. At all relevant times, the top 7 (seven) officials of PWD including the petitioner were under consideration for promotion for the post of Chief Engineer. In this regard, a circular dated 2-9-1991 issued by the then Ministry of Establishment is relevant, which categorically provides, inter alia, that a minimum number of 5(five) personnel should be proposed to the SSB for promotion for each vacant post. In compliance, with the aforesaid Circular dated 2-9-1991 the respondent No. 1 issued a Memo being No. 25.018.005.02.00.002.2013-323 dated 5-8-2013 stating, amongst others, that there are no allegations of any misconduct or any pending cases against the petitioner. It is further stated that the Ministry of Public Administration vide letter No. 05.133.012.233.205.02.2013-244 dated 10-10-2013 had asked the respondent No. 1 to send a proper proposal for promotion in compliance with the circular dated 2-9-1991 along with approved gradation list and the organogram categorically stating, inter alia that there was substantial discrepancies and mistakes in the earlier proposal dated 9-10-2013 (Annexures I, I-1 and 1-2). 

 9. The respondent No. 5 by the Memo being No. 05.133.006.05.01.01.2013-244 dated 9-10-2013 issued a notice for the 11th (Eleventh) Meeting of SSB for the year 2013 to be held on 20-10-2013. It is pertinent to note here that promotion for the post of Chief Engineer under PWD was not included as an agenda in the said meeting. However, the petitioner learnt from a reliable source that the promotion for the post of Chief Engineer under PWD was also taken up for consideration in the said meeting of SSB held on 20-10-2013, although it was not initially made an agenda for the said meeting. From the aforesaid actions of the respondents, it is evident that the respondents at the behest of a vested quarter are bent upon in promoting a particular individual, namely, the said Current Charge-holder, as Chief Engineer of PWD inspite of the fact that the said Current Charge-holder is enlisted at Serial No. 133 in the Gradation List and thus there are 6(six) other personnel, including the petitioner who is enlisted at Serial No. 128 of the Gradation List, who are senior to the said Current Charge-holder (Annexure- J). 

 10. It is stated that as per the seniority list of Additional Chief Engineer of PWD, the petitioner is at Serial No. 3 against the said Current Charge-holder's Serial No. 7, who is now holding the post of Chief Engineer on Current Charge. 

 11. Serial No. 1, Column No. 4 of Part XII of the Bangladesh Civil Service recruitment Rules, 1981 ("the Rules 1981") provides that the vacant post of Chief Engineer under PWD shall be filled by way of promotion from amongst the Additional Chief Engineers having a total service experience of 18 (Eighteen) years including 3 (three) years’ experience as Additional Chief Engineer and in the meantime, the petitioner has completed about 34 (thirty four) years of service with an unblemished record. It is pertinent to note here that the petitioner has already completed more than 2(two) years and 11 (eleven) months in his service as Additional Chief Engineer, while the said Current Charge-holder has only completed, only about 02(two) years and 3(three) months in his service as Additional Chief Engineer (Annexure-K). 

 12. It is stated that as per Circular dated 5-2-1992, issued by the then Ministry of Establishment, the order of Current Charge shall be made on the basis of seniority/gradation list and accordingly, the assigning of the said Current Charge-holder with the post of Chief Engineer (Current Charge) under PWD is not tenable in law. 

 13. The respondent No. 1 contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition and contended inter alia that the post of Chief Engineer has been vacant since 17-8-2011. Government considering all the factors for promotion, Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan, Additional Chief Engineer has been given the charge as Chief Engineer in the Current Charge vide Memo No. GriGoMo/Sha-1/SA-3/2009/91 dated 17-8-2011 & Memo No. GriGoMo/Sha-1/4P-1/2011/104 dated 22-9-11. The petitioner is not the senior most among the Additional Chief Engineers. Chief Engineer post is the post of head of the Department and policy making Government, so considering the previous service records & performance of Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan is entrusted with the responsibility of Chief Engineer for the betterment of the Department. In BCS Public Works, recruitment Rules, the criteria of promotion for the cost of Chief Engineer is to have 18 years service with at least 3 years as Additional Chief Engineer in the feeder post on the basis of seniority. 

 14. The Government considering all facts found Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan as the finest candidate amongst the Additional Chief Engineers and thus has given him the current charge of Chief Engineer, who has been promoted to the rank of Additional Chief Engineer on 25013.012.05.003.2010-69 dated 30-6-201. 

 15. The Ministry of Housing and Public Works vide Memo No.25.00.0000.013.12.001.09-678 dated 9-10-2013 send proposal to the Superior Service Selection Board (SSB) proposing the name of Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan for promotion to the post of Chief Engineer, considering the services rendered by him for last 2 years. He is running the department very efficiently and made expansion of the department by creating huge number of posts in different level. Considering the previous service career, he is doing better for the department in the given current charge for the post of Chief Engineer, while other addition Chief Engineers are working, under him for more than two years. On considering his performance for running the PWD smoothly and efficiently for 2 years, the Ministry has proposed his name to the SSB. BCS Public Works Recruitment Rule, criteria for promotion to Chief Engineer is "Amongst the Additional Chief Engineer" with 18 years' with 3 years' service in the feeder post. For promotion to the top post only seniority is not the basis of promotion. Government should consider the capability, efficiency and his previous service-records; even in the past seniority have never been the criteria for pro-motion to the post of Chief Engineer. 

 18. The Government considering Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan, fit for the post of Chief Engineer, for the betterment of the department, as the respondent No. 6, at present is in the current charge at the post of Chief Engineer and he is running the department in a very well manner, and since he has served in the post for last 2 years while all other Additional Chief Engineers are working under him. 

 20. The respondent No. 2 contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition, and stated inter alia that the Ministry of Housing and Public Works as the Administrative Ministry forwarded a proposal dated 9-10-2013 in the form of summary for promotion containing only one name that of Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuyian Additional Chief Engineer. But the set Rule regarding submission of proposal for promotion to be placed before the Superior Selection Board (SSB) directs to send at least 5 names and other necessary particulars against 1 post. Subsequently, the Ministry of Housing and Public Works vide their letter dated 20-10-2013 submitted a revised proposal containing 7 names and particulars of possible candidates for the promotion to the post of Chief Engineer, PWD. Since the proposal dated 9-10-2013 was not acted upon, therefore the writ petition is liable to be discharged. 

 21. On 20-10-2013, SSB discussed the matter of promotion to the post of Chief Engineer of PWD on the basis of agenda No. 16 (Miscellaneous) of the said notice. A total of 7(seven) persons were proposed for consideration for the promotion of 1 position. According to the proposal of the Ministry of Housing and Public Works Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan had been found eligible by SSB for promotion to the post of Chief Engineer, PWD, since 5 others including the petitioner hand shortcomings in ACR and 1 other was working on deputation in RAJUK. In addition, the members of the SSB were of opinion that more information was required regarding the satisfactory service record of those 6 officers. And Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan, Additional Chief Engineer, PWD was recommended for promotion to the Post of Chief Engineer, PWD subject to condonation of service length by the President of the Republic. 

 22. Although the petitioner is at serial number 3 in the seniority list while Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan, is at serial No. 7 but all other 6 candidates including the petitioner hand shortcoming in the Annual Confidential Report (ACR), which is very crucial for taking decision regarding such promotion cases. The post of Chief Engineer, PWD fell vacant on 11-8-2010 and this department involves many important public works for which Md Kabir Ahmed was assigned with the Additional Charge as the Chief Engineer, PWD. It is a fact that Bangladesh Civil Service Recruitment Rules, 1981 provides that the vacant post of Chief Engineer, PWD shall be filed tip by way of promotion from amongst the Additional Chief Engineers having a total service experience of 18 years including 3 years’ experience as Additional Chief Engineer. Md Kabir Ahmed did not fulfil the requirement of 3 years’ experience as Additional Chief Engineer for which the SSB left the issue of service length condonation under the good conscience of the President. 

 24. The petitioner misconceived and misled the actual fact. The fact remains that the Ministry of Housing and Public Works as the Administrative Ministry forwarded a proposal dated 9-10-2013 in the form of summary for promotion containing only one name and particulars that of Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan, Additional Chief Engineer. But the set Rule regarding submission of proposal for promotion to be placed before the Superior Selection Board (SSB) is to send at least 5 names against 1 post, unless otherwise. Subsequently the Ministry of Housing and Public Works vide their letter dated 20-10-2013 submitted a revised proposal containing 7 names and particulars of possible candidates for the promotion to the post of Chief Engineer, PWD. 

 26. The respondent No. 6 contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition contending that the petitioner is an Additional Chief Engineer of the Department of Public Works and he being a Government Employee cannot file this writ petition raising disputes regarding his promotion, which clearly falls within the terms and condition of service, as such, the Rule is not maintainable and hence the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 27. Seniority is not the only basis for which the petitioner can claim legitimate expectation to be promoted to the post of Chief Engineer of PWD. 

 28. The post of Chief Engineer has been vacant since 17-8-2011. The respondent No. 1 considering the efficiency, competency and previous brilliant service record of respondent No. 6, is bestowed with charge of Chief Engineer (current charge) vide memo No- Gri GoMo/Sha-1/ SA-3/2009/91 dated 17-8-2011 & Memo No- GriGoMo/Sha-1/4p-1/2011/104 dated 22-9-11. 

 29. The respondent No. 6 was transferred as Director (Current Charge) of Housing and Building Research Institute, Darusalam, Mirpur; Khandaker Salauddin (Gradation No. 127) was posted as Chief Engineer (Current Charge) superseding his senior Fazlul Kader (Gradation No. 112) and subsequently the respondent No.1 vide notification No. 25.013.011.05.00.003.2009-09 dated 28-1-2013, again posted the respondent No. 6 as Chief Engineer (Current Charge). 

 30. The respondent No. 1, Ministry of Housing and Public Works vide memo No. 25.00.0000.013.12.001.09-678 dated 9-10-2013 considering the services rendered by respondent No. 6 in last 2 years as Chief Engineer (Current Charge) and fulfilling other criterion for promotion sent summary to the SSB proposing the name of the respondent No. 6 for promotion to the post of Chief Engineer. Thereafter the respondent No. 2 vide memo No. 05.133.012.233.205.02.2013-244 dated 10-10-2013 asked the respondent No. 1 to send fresh proposal fulfilling the conditions as stated in office order as contained in Memo being No. 05.133.012.233.205.02.2013-244 dated 10-10-2013 issued by respondent No. 2. In compliance with the said Memo dated 10-10-2013 respondent No. 1 sent a fresh proposal containing 7(seven) names including the name of the petitioner and respondent No. 6 and all other information as sought for vide letter as contained in SSB memo No. 25.00.0000.013.012.005.09.700 dated 20-10-2013. 

 31. The respondent No. 5 circulated a notice on 9-10-2013 of 11th meetings of the SSB to be held on 20-10-2013. The respondent No. 1 on 9-10-2013 sent a summary for the promotion to the post of Chief Engineer. On receipt of the summary the respondent No. 2 asked the respondent No. 1 to send fresh proposal following the circular of the Ministry of Public Administration dated 2-9-1991. Thereafter in compliance to the letter the respondent No. 1 on 20-10-2013 sent a fresh proposal containing seven names of Additional Chief Engineers including the name of the petitioner for consideration of the SSB to be held on 20-10-2013. Though the petitioner challenged the summary dated 9-10-2013 for not sending his name in the said summary, but on 20-10-2013 a fresh proposal has been sent including the name of the petitioner, and Rule has been issued on 24-10-2013 as such, the Rule has become infructuous and considering efficiency and previous brilliant service record of the respondent No. 6, respondent No. 1 the gave him the current charge of Chief Engineer on 17-8-2011 and he has been performing his duties efficiently and satisfactorily for last 2 years and all the Additional Chief Engineers including the petitioner are working under him without any grievance. 

 32. The respondent No. 6 obtained his graduation in Civil Engineering, securing 1st, Class 3rd position from the University of Chittagong in the year 1978. Thereafter he joined as. Assistant Engineer in the Department of Public Works on 10-3-1979 and subsequently he was promoted to the post of Sub Divisional Engineer in 1983. He was thereafter promoted as Executive Engineer on 22-3-2001 and Superintending Engineer on 13-9-2009. In recognition of his efficient and meritorious service he was promoted to the post of Additional Chief Engineer on 30-6-2011 (Annexures-1, 2, 3, 4 and 5). 

 49. Which very conspicuously resembles that while by attaining 92.75 marks the instant petitioner stood at first position against Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuyian, respondent No. 6, with 93.40 marks who stood at fourth position as yet, without any negative stigma and with the highest ACR points, the petitioner was deprived of the right to promotion and very discriminatorily, the name of respondent No. 6 name was included and proposed for promotion and he was given current charge of the Chief Engineer by passing 6 of his seniors. 

 50. He further submitted that promotion is an advancement in career and an employee joins in any service seeing the promotional opportunity in future and denial of promotion always create frustration in his mind, which is also violative of his fundamental rights guaranteed under Article 29 of the Constitution, inasmuch as, promotions are made available in every wings of service to bring efficiency in the service and to foster appropriate attitude to grow for the purpose of achieving excellence, therefore failure to make promotion of the senior like the petitioner will certainly lead to degeneration and stagnation, thereby destroying the urge of work of the others in the department, as such, the respondents may kindly be directed to make promotion in the post of Chief Engineer (PWD) on the basis of seniority. 

 52. Mr Dolon, further submitted that the impugned memo dated 9-10-2013 is arbitrary, malafide, unreasonable inasmuch as the respondents at the behest of a vested quarter are bent upon in promoting a particular individual as Chief Engineer of the PWD, in spite of the fact that, the said Current Charge-holder is enlisted at Serial No. 133 in the Gradation List and thus there are 6(Six) other personnel (including the petitioner who is enlisted a Serial No. 128 of the Gradation List, who are senior to the said Current Charge-holder. 

 57. Mr MK Rahman, the learned Additional Attorney-General, with Mr Biswojit Roy, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, appearing for the respondent No. 1, submitted that the Ministry of Housing and Public Works as the Administrative Ministry forwarded a proposal dated 9-10-2013 in the form of summary for promotion containing only one name that of Md Kabir Ahmed Bhuyian, Additional Chief Engineer. But the set Rule regarding submission of proposal for promotion to be placed before the Superior Selection Board (SSB) directs to send at least 5 names and other necessary particulars against 1 post. Subsequently, the Ministry of Housing and Public Works vide their letter dated 20-10-2013 submitted a revised proposal containing 7 names and particulars of possible candidates for the promotion to the post of Chief Engineer, PWD. Since the proposal dated 9-10-2013 was not acted upon, therefore the writ petition is liable to be discharged. 

 59. Mr Shafique Ahmed, the learned Senior Advocate with Mr SM Rezaul Karim, and Mr Mahabub Shafique, Advocates, appearing for the respondent No.6, submitted that the petitioner is an Additional Chief Engineer of the Department of Public Works and he being a Government Employee cannot file this writ petition raising disputes regarding the promotion, which clearly falls within the terms and condition of service, as such, the Rule is not maintainable and hence the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 61. He further submitted that seniority is not the only basis for which the petitioner can claim legitimate expectation to be promoted to the post of Chief Engineer of PWD. The post of Chief Engineer has been vacant since 17-8-2011. The respondent No.1 considering the efficiency, competency and previous brilliant service record of respondent No. 6, is bestowed with charge of Chief Engineer (current charge) vide memo No. Gri GoMo/Sha-1 /SA-3 /2009 /91 dated 17-8-2011 & Memo No- Gri GoMo /Sha-1/4p-1/2011/104 date 22-9-11. 

 62. He further submitted that the respondent No. 6 was transferred as Director (Current Charge) of Housing and Building Research Institute, Darusalam, Mirpur; Khandaker Salauddin (Gradation No. 127) and was posted as Chief Engineer (Current Charge) superseding his senior Fazlul Kader (Gradation No. 112) and subsequently the respondent No.1 vide notification No. 25.013.011.05.00.003.2009-09 dated 28-1-2013, again posted the respondent No. 6 as Chief Engineer (Current-Charge) of the PWD. 

 63. Mr Ahmed, further submitted that the respondent No.1, Ministry Housing and Public Works vide memo No-25.00.0000.013.12.001.09-678 dated 9-10-2013 considering the services rendered by respondent No. 6 in last 2 years as Chief Engineer (Current-Charge) and fulfilling other criterion for promotion sent summary to the SSB proposing the name of the respondent No. 6 for promotion to the post of Chief Engineer. Thereafter the respondent No. 2 vide memo No. 05.133.012.233.205.02.2013-244 dated 10-10-2013 asked the respondent No. 1 to send fresh proposal fulfilling the conditions as stated in office order as contained in Memo being No. 05.133.012.233.205.02.2013-244 dated 10-10-2013 issued by respondent No.2. In compliance with the said Memo dated 10-10-2013 respondent No. 1 sent a fresh proposal containing 7(seven) names including the name of the petitioner and respondent No. 6 and all other information as sought for vide letter as contained in SSB memo No-25.00.0000.013.012.005.09.700 dated 20-10-2013. 

 64. He again submitted that the respondent No. 5 circulated a notice on 9-10-2013 of 11th meetings of the SSB to be held on 20-10- 2013.The respondent No. 1 on 9-10-2013 sent a summary for the promotion to the post of Chief Engineer. On receipt of the summary the respondent No. 2 asked the respondent No. 1 to send fresh proposal following the circular of the Ministry of Public Administration dated 2-9-1991. Thereafter in compliance to the letter the respondent No. 1 on 20-10-2013, sent a fresh proposal containing 7 names of the Additional Chief Engineers including the name of the petitioner for consideration of the SSB to be held on 20-10-2013. Though the petitioner challenged the summary dated 9-10-2013 for not sending his name in the said summary, but on 20-10-2013 a fresh proposal has been sent including the name of the petitioner, and Rule has been issued on 24-10-2013, as such, the Rule has become infructuous and considering efficiency and previous brilliant service record of the respondent No. 6, respondent No. 1, gave him the current charge of Chief Engineer on 17-8-2011 and he has been performing his duties efficiently and satisfactorily for last 2 years and all the Additional Chief Engineers including the petitioner are working under him without any grievance. 

 65. He further submitted that the respondent No. 6 obtained his graduation in Civil Engineering, securing 1st Class 3rd position from the University of Chittagong in the year 1978. Thereafter he joined as Assistant Engineer in the Department of Public Works on 10-3-1979 and subsequently he was promoted to the post of Sub Divisional Engineer in 1983. He was thereafter promoted as Executive Engineer on 22-3-2001 and Superintending Engineer on 13-9-2009. In recognition of his efficient and meritorious service he was promoted to the post of Additional Chief Engineer on 30-6-2011 (Annexure-1, 2, 3, 4 and 5). 

 66. On perusal of the submission of both the parties, the petition, the affidavit-in-opposition and the available documents, it is quite apparent note that the authority concerned for filling up the vacancy of the Chief No. 6 for promotion to the said post as a single candidate for perusal of the Superior Service Selection Board (SSB) by Memo No. ২৫.০০.০০০০.০১৩.১২.০০১.০৯.৬৭৮ তারিখঃ ৯ অক্টোবর ২০১৩ (Annexure-H). And that memo has been sent back by the Ministry of Public Administration by order dated 10-10-2013 vide Memo No. ০৫.১৩৩.০১২.২৩৩.২৫.০২.২০১৩-২৪৪ (Annexure 1-2) thereafter vide Memo No. ২৫.০০.০০০০.০১৩.১২.০০১.০৯.৬৭৮ তারিখঃ ৯ অক্টোবর ২০১৩ (Annexure-13) names of 7(seven) Additional Chief Engineers were sent for consideration, wherein name of the respondent No. 6 was included, who at that time did not have the requisite qualification in service, i.e. 3(three) years’ experience in the feeder post. In fact none of the said 7(seven) candidates had the 3(three) years’ experience in the feeder post for which condonation from the fitness of the President of the Republic was required as per notification dated 1-1-1991 of the Establishment Division (Regulation Wing, Cabinet Secretariat). The proposal sent to the SSB on 20-10-2013, proposed the condonation for relaxation under Article-k8 of the notification dated 1-1-1991, was sought only for the respondent No. 6, while condonation ought to have been sought for all the candidates or in the alternative that condonation ought to have been kept open only for the person to whom the SSB gives recommendation for promotion, instead proposing recommendation for the same person not having fulfilled 3(three) years in the feeder post bypassing the 6(six) seniors and the concerned public authority's previous conduct of sending single name for promotion to the SSB by passing 6(six) seniors and without tabling gradation list before the SSB seriously portrays, mala fide and malicious conduct of the concerned public authority of biasness in favour of a single candidate, i.e. respondent No. 6. In such view of the matter, we are of the view that such a proposal superseding 6(six) seniors while the requirement was to send at least 5(five) names, that was done only to favour a single person, i.e. the respondent No. 6, is nothing but biasness, malicious, mala fide and colourable exercise of power, on part of the public authority. The whole process from the beginning of sending a single name thereafter on its rejection sending 7(seven) names including the name of the respondent No. 6 clearly resembles that, the concerned public authority pre-determined to promote respondent No. 6 to the post of Chief Engineer. 

 67. The contesting respondents have stated that the ACR of the 6 other Additional Chief Engineers, except the ACR of the respondent No. 6 was not satisfactory, but on perusal of the relevant papers, it clearly resembles that none of the ACRs had any stigma upon any of the seven, rather it is quite apparent that in the ACR markings the petitioner stood in the position with 9-2-75 marks as against the respondent No. 6, securing only 93.40 marks in serial No. 4, in terms of merit. 

 68. While 6 senior officers are quite ably competent, even than superseding them giving charge of Chief Engineer to the 7th person in the list of seniority, itself is a flagrant violation of natural justice forcing the said 6 seniors to serve under the junior most Additional Chief Engineer. It clearly portrays that the authority did not treat all its employees equally. In AKM Kawser Ahmed vs Bangladesh, 65 DLR 377, it was observed inter alia that: 

 69. In the instant case the concerned public authority has utterly failed to act fairly, which quite apparent from the submissions of the petitioner and, as well as, respondents, since the respondents could not show any justification with regard to proposing the name of the respondent No. 6 for promotion superseding 6 other Additional Chief Engineers, who did not at all stood in any better standing than to the petitioner, therefore the Rule deserves merit. 

 In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the proposal send by the Ministry of Housing and Public Works for promotion to the post of Chief Engineer from amongst the proposed 7 candidate including the respondent Nos. 6 and 7 is hereby declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The respondents Nos. 1- 4 are hereby directed to make proposal of 5(fives) senior most Additional Chief Engineers to the SSB without any special favour in favour of any particular candidate and to promote the most eligible candidate in terms of qualification, seniority and experience, on the basis of the ACR within 15 days of receipt of this judgment and order.
